title: What drives disaster risk across Tanzania
lead: A guided tour of the INFORM Risk Index for every council and region: where risk concentrates, which hazards dominate, what drives the scores, and how complete the evidence is.

regions.title: How the regions compare
regions.lead: Regions are built from their councils the INFORM way, not by averaging risk scores. Switch the measure to see each dimension against its own class thresholds.
regions.chartSub: Colour = INFORM class · dashed line = national value
regions.aria: Bar chart of regions ranked by {{measure}}. The highest is {{top}} at {{value}}.
regions.caption: The national line is Tanzania’s official INFORM value, not an average of the regions. Select a bar to open a region’s profile.

scatter.title: Where hazard meets vulnerability
scatter.lead: Every bubble is a council. Risk is highest where hazard and vulnerability are both high and the capacity to cope is weak.
scatter.chartSub: Colour = INFORM Risk class · size = population · dashed lines = class thresholds
scatter.aria_one: Scatter plot of {{total}} councils by hazard and vulnerability; {{count}} council falls in the high-hazard, high-vulnerability corner.
scatter.aria_other: Scatter plot of {{total}} councils by hazard and vulnerability; {{count}} councils fall in the high-hazard, high-vulnerability corner.
scatter.caption: The shaded corner (hazard ≥ {{h}}, vulnerability ≥ {{v}}) is where the High classes of both dimensions overlap. Colour also reflects the lack of coping capacity, so neighbouring bubbles can differ.
scatter.hotBody: These councils combine High hazard (≥ {{h}}) with High vulnerability (≥ {{v}}) and are home to {{pop}} people.

matrix.title: Which hazards dominate where
matrix.lead: Average natural-hazard scores for every region. Sort by any hazard to find its hot-spots.
matrix.chartSub: Average score, 0–10 · darker = more severe · select a column heading to sort
matrix.tableCaption: Average natural-hazard indicator scores by region, from 0 to 10.
matrix.caption: Read along a row for a region’s hazard profile, or down a column to see where a hazard concentrates. 10 is the most severe value in Tanzania’s data.

classes.title: How risk is spread within each region
classes.lead: A regional score can hide variation. This view counts the councils in each INFORM Risk class, region by region.
classes.chartTitle: Councils by risk class, per region
classes.chartSub: Share of councils in each class · figure = share at High or above
classes.aria: {{all}} of {{total}} regions have every council at High risk or above; {{none}} have none.
classes.caption: Shares rather than counts let regions of different sizes compare fairly. Mixed bars show where targeting within a region matters most.
classes.allHigh_one: region has every council at High risk or above
classes.allHigh_other: regions have every council at High risk or above
classes.noneHigh_one: region has no council at High risk
classes.noneHigh_other: regions have no council at High risk

drivers.title: The indicator groups behind the scores
drivers.lead: Which single indicator scores highest in each council, and how every indicator averages out nationally.
drivers.countSub: Number of councils (out of {{total}}) where each indicator scores highest
drivers.countCaption_one: {{indicator}} is the top-scoring indicator in {{count}} council ({{pct}}). When several indicators tie for the top score each one is counted, so the bars can add up to more than the number of councils.
drivers.countCaption_other: {{indicator}} is the top-scoring indicator in {{count}} councils ({{pct}}). When several indicators tie for the top score each one is counted, so the bars can add up to more than the number of councils.
drivers.meanSub: Mean across councils, grouped by dimension (0–10)
drivers.noData: No sub-national data yet for this indicator.
drivers.uniform: Same value in every council (for example, a national baseline).
drivers.meanCaption: Long bars are structural weaknesses shared across the country: {{indicator}} ({{dimension}}) has the highest national average, at {{value}}. Short bars can still matter a great deal in the few councils where they are high.

coverage.title: How complete, and how local, is the evidence?
coverage.lead: How many indicators each council has values for, and at what geographic level each indicator is measured.
coverage.histSub: Share of the {{total}} indicator groups with a value, per council
coverage.histCaption: Missing values are left out of the averages, never counted as zero. Gaps come from indicators that have no sub-national source yet.
coverage.resTitle: Where each indicator’s data comes from
coverage.resSub: Geographic resolution of the source behind every indicator

resDesc.council: Computed for each council’s own area
resDesc.region: Survey data available per region only
resDesc.national: The same national value for every council (INFORM SADC 2024)
resDesc.overlay: Mapped from documented hazard zones and events

coverage.resCaption: {{local}} of {{total}} indicator groups ({{pct}}) are measured locally, at council or district level.
coverage.honestTitle: An honest note on data gaps
coverage.honestBody: {{national}} of the {{total}} indicator groups still use a national baseline and {{overlay}} are documented overlays, while {{region}} rely on region-level surveys. These layers cannot tell councils apart as sharply as local data can, so differences between neighbouring councils mostly reflect hazard and exposure. They will be replaced as ministries and agencies submit council-level data through the Data portal.

correlation.title: How the dimensions move together
correlation.lead: Pearson correlations across councils show whether places that score high on one dimension also score high on another.
correlation.chartTitle: Correlations between the three dimensions and risk
correlation.caption: Red cells: the two measures rise together. Blue cells: one tends to fall as the other rises. Neutral cells: little relationship. Correlation describes a pattern, not a cause.
correlation.findingRisk: {{dim}} moves most closely with overall risk (r = {{r}}).
correlation.findingHvLow: Hazard and vulnerability are largely independent (r = {{r}}): the most hazard-exposed councils are not the most vulnerable ones, so risk is spread across the country rather than concentrated in one place.
correlation.findingHvHigh: Hazard and vulnerability rise together (r = {{r}}): the most hazard-exposed councils also tend to be the most vulnerable, which concentrates risk.
correlation.note: Based on {{n}} councils. Vulnerability and coping values come from the {{sources}} INFORM source units, so councils that share a source unit share those values.

notes.title: About these figures
notes.national: The national value is the official INFORM figure for Tanzania, not an average of councils or regions.
notes.regions: Regional values are aggregated from their councils the INFORM way: indicator group averages → category averages → dimension scores → risk as the cube root of hazard × vulnerability × lack of coping capacity.
notes.thresholds: Each dimension has its own class thresholds. For overall risk the classes are {{ranges}} (Very low → Very high).
notes.councils: Each council has its own hazard and exposure; vulnerability and coping come from its INFORM source unit, because survey data has no council breakdown.
